steps.name: Sample structure QC and shallow-sample verdict
caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.
With only 6 per group, dropping sample_01 costs real power; weigh that against whatever the plots show.

steps.description: Read /eval-four-models-v2-with-mouse-two-group-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, gene ids in the first column) and metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition). steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test, HFD vs chow, with apeglm shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. These counts come from Salmon as a gene-level table with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, so the import state is not established. Fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not invent a length input.
With 6 replicates per group DESeq2 flags count outliers by Cook's distance and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing the counts; report those genes rather than losing them silently.
If T1S1 dropped sample_01, the treated/control group sizes become unequal and the pre-filter min_samples should follow the new smallest group size; state the change.
steps.context: 6 high-fat-diet vs 6 chow mouse liver samples (or 5 vs 6 if T1S1 dropped sample_01 with a stated reason), unpaired, single batch, 12,000 genes before filtering. Counts are gene-level Salmon output with mouse gene symbols.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed in mouse liver between high-fat diet and chow, at BH-adjusted p < 0.05, and how many of them does an independent second method (edgeR quasi-likelihood) also call?

steps.description: Using the sample set decided in T1S1, build a DESeqDataSet from the raw counts with design ~condition. Set the reference level of condition explicitly to the chow/control level (do not rely on alphabetical ordering) and name the contrast as condition, HFD numerator, chow denominator, so a positive log2 fold change means higher in high-fat diet. Run DESeq() — median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside the model, so do not pre-normalize. Extract results with alpha=0.05 and independent filtering on, inspect the histogram of unadjusted p-values before trusting the adjustment, and adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg. Report the number of genes with NA adjusted p-value from the Cook's-distance count-outlier flag separately from those the independent filter removed (with 6 per group DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers). constraints: Rank on the full list of tested genes; do not cut the list at an adjusted p-value or fold change before the test

Use the mouse MSigDB hallmark collection directly — do not map mouse symbols to human orthologs and use a human collection
Set size window: min 15, max 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Adjust set p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg; set and report a random seed

steps.description: Take the full T1S2 results table — every tested gene, not a thresholded subset — and rank it by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column). Run fgsea against the mouse hallmark gene set collection from the reference store: the MSigDB mouse hallmark GMT, mouse symbols (MGI), which matches the gene symbols in counts.csv directly, so no ortholog mapping is required and none should be performed. Resolve the collection by what it is (mouse hallmark gene sets) rather than by a hardcoded path, and record its release. Apply a set size window of 15 to 500 members after intersecting each set with the tested genes, adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg, set and record a random seed for the permutations. Report normalized enrichment score, p-value, adjusted p-value, set size and leading-edge genes per set, and mark the leading-edge overlap between the reported sets; collapse redundant sets (fgsea collapsePathways) and give one representative per group with the full table as a supplement. steps.description: Assemble the results of T1S2 and T2S1 into one report. Lead with the counts: genes tested after filtering, genes with padj < 0.05 in the HFD vs chow contrast, and significant hallmark sets. plan.title: HFD vs chow mouse liver DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, 13 columns = gene id + 12 samples) from Salmon with mouse gene symbols, plus metadata.csv (12 rows, sample + condition), for 6 high-fat-diet vs 6 chow mouse liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question asks two things — which genes change and which hallmark pathways change — plus explicit handling of one shallow sample (sample_01, library size ~4x below the median).

T1S1 runs the sample-structure QC on raw counts: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap, and a per-sample library-size / detected-gene table. sample_01 is kept through QC and judged on those plots rather than dropped for depth alone — DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth, and a low-depth sample simply carries wider intervals. Removal is only warranted with a stated non-depth reason (e.g. it does not group with its condition and shows a degraded distribution); the step must state the decision either way and, if it drops the sample, the downstream test is refit at n=5 vs 6 with that stated.

T1S2 fits DESeq2 with design ~condition, reference level chow set explicitly, contrast condition HFD vs chow, after a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size). Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. One caveat is load-bearing: the profile records the counts as gene-level Salmon output with no statement about whether the length correction was applied, and no quant.sf files or average-transcript-length table are present in the inputs. The model therefore runs on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and the report must state that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can appear as differential expression. tximport is not run — it imports transcript-level estimates, not a gene table. edgeR quasi-likelihood is run as a second method on the same counts and design so the report can give the overlap as the high-confidence set.

T2S1 answers the pathway half: fgsea preranked on the full list of tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking-metric choice is resolved in favour of the Wald stat — it is signed and scaled by its standard error, unlike an unshrunken fold change), against the mouse MSigDB hallmark collection, which is staged in the reference store (mouse symbols, matching the MGI symbols in counts.csv — no ortholog mapping needed and none should be invented). Set size window 15-500 after intersection with the tested genes, BH adjustment, redundant sets collapsed, leading edge reported per significant set. WikiPathways mouse is also staged and is run as a second collection, tested separately rather than merged, with each release stated.

T1S3 consolidates: MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, gene table carrying unshrunken and shrunken log2FC with lfcSE, DESeq2/edgeR overlap, hallmark and WikiPathways results with their releases and the ranking metric, and the full reproducibility record. With 6 vs 6 and 12,000 genes this design has reasonable power for moderate effects; the report should not present hallmark sets as mechanism, only as coordinated-change hypotheses.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size report
~ condition with explicit reference level chow
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against mouse MSigDB Hallmark
consolidated DE + GSEA report with fit diagnostics and reproducibility record

Mouse hallmark collection used with its release recorded; no mouse-to-human symbol mapping performed
Result table per collection with pathway, NES, pval, BH padj, size and leading-edge genes
Redundant sets collapsed, with one representative per group reported and the full table retained
WikiPathways mouse reported as a separate table with its own release, not merged with hallmark
Share of tested genes matching at least one gene set reported, and the random seed recorded
constraints: Rank on the full list of tested genes; do not cut the list at an adjusted p-value or fold change before the test

Rank metric = the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat). This resolves the disputed ranking-metric choice: the Wald statistic is signed and scaled by its standard error, unlike the unshrunken log2 fold change, and it has no ties at zero as a signed p-value would
Use the mouse MSigDB hallmark collection directly — do not map mouse symbols to human orthologs and use a human collection
Set size window: min 15, max 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Adjust set p-values with Benjamini-Hochberg; set and report a random seed
Test each collection separately with the same universe and size window; never concatenate hallmark and WikiPathways into one set list
caveats: The number of individually significant genes is not known in advance. If it falls below about 50, do not fall back to an over-representation test on that short list — the ranked test on the full list is the correct method here and is already what this step runs.
Enrichment results depend on the method: present significant sets as hypotheses supported by coordinated change, not as demonstrated mechanism.
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment; the universe is the set of tested genes, and that should be stated.

grounding.reason: Ranked-list enrichment after a DESeq2 contrast on mouse data: fgsea preranked against the mouse MSigDB hallmark collection per R-0107@976c and R-0049@d76b, with WikiPathways mouse as the further collection per R-0165@e456. Disputed rule R-0108@409f is resolved on the Wald statistic side: it is signed and scaled by its standard error and does not saturate into ties.

steps.name: Consolidated DE and hallmark report
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes and which hallmark pathways change between high-fat diet and chow mouse liver', and what are the limits of that answer given one shallow sample and an unestablished length correction?
steps.description: Assemble the results of T1S2 and T2S1 into one report. Lead with the counts: genes tested after filtering, genes with padj < 0.05 in the HFD vs chow contrast, and significant hallmark sets. Give the gene table ranked by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change, carrying the unshrunken log2FoldChange, the shrunken value, lfcSE, stat, pvalue and padj, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header. Include the fit diagnostics: MA plot and dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit, plus the p-value histogram, each with a sentence on what it shows. Report the DESeq2 / edgeR overlap, treating the intersection as the high-confidence set and listing method-unique genes as secondary. For the pathway half, report hallmark and WikiPathways separately with each collection's release, the ranking metric (DESeq2 Wald statistic), the universe (tested genes), the size window, the tool version and the multiple-testing method, plus the leading-edge genes of each significant set and their overlaps. State plainly the three limits of this analysis: sample_01's depth and the verdict taken on it; that the Salmon gene-level counts carry no length offset, so an isoform-usage shift can present as differential expression; and that enrichment results are method-dependent, so a hallmark set is a hypothesis for follow-up rather than an established mechanism. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seeds, and collection releases, stored with the results.
steps.context: Final synthesis for the high-fat diet vs chow mouse liver bulk RNA-seq analysis. All numbers come from T1S2 and T2S1; this step computes no new test.
acceptance_criteria: Report states method, package versions, design formula, the contrast as condition HFD vs chow, thresholds, genes tested, and genes significant
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, ranked by the shrunken value
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included, each with an interpretation line
DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap reported with intersection treated as the high-confidence set
Hallmark and WikiPathways results reported separately with release, ranking metric, universe, size window and leading-edge genes
The three stated limitations appear explicitly: sample_01 verdict, missing length offset, enrichment method dependence
Reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, collection releases) stored with the results
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit unchanged
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Do not claim mechanism from an enriched hallmark set
No new statistical test is fitted in this step
caveats: With 6 per group (or 5 vs 6 if sample_01 was dropped), the study is powered for moderate to large effects only; say so rather than implying an absence of signal is an absence of biology.

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as a whole; its content follows the reporting claims R-0085, R-0087, R-0042, R-0041, R-0051, R-0055, R-0105 and R-0086.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
